title: Zero-germ detection for a local morphism from a finite type source
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, $\mathcal F$ a finite type module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], $\mathcal G$ any module sheaf, $x\in U$ with $U$ open, and $\varphi\in\mathcal Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)(U)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Suppose that for every open $V\subseteq U$ containing $x$ and every $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, the germ at $x$ of $\varphi_V(s)$ is zero in $\mathcal G_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then the germ $\varphi_x$ is zero in $\mathcal Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)_x$.

source.place: Tag 01CP, proof, second paragraph (finite type injectivity).

proof.text: Choose an open neighborhood of x with finitely many generating sections for F, and intersect it with U. The restricted sections still generate: restriction to a smaller slice is exact and preserves the free generator epimorphism.

Apply the hypothesis to each restricted generator. Its image has zero germ. For each generator, the definition of equality of germs supplies a smaller neighborhood on which its image is zero; take the finite intersection of these neighborhoods.

The restricted local morphism vanishes on the generators, so its composite with their free epimorphism is zero. Cancel that epimorphism to conclude that the restricted morphism is zero. Taking its germ gives the original germ by restriction compatibility, so the original germ is zero. The empty family gives a zero source and the same cancellation argument.

A germ of a local sheaf morphism from a finite type module sheaf is zero if its induced stalk linear map is zero
